To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
The rate of cell production in the inner enamel epithelial stem cell compartment of the rat incisors is directly related to the rate of eruption and is regulated by the rate of tooth eruption.

the inner enamel epithelial (IEE) cell cycle of the continuously growing rat incisor is a function of the rate of eruption and that the IEE cell cycle is a linear function of the rate at which cells are added to the IEE cell pool.

the rate of cell proliferation in the inner enamel epithelial cell compartment is linearly related to the rate of tooth eruption, and that the rate of tooth movement is a function of the rate of cell division in the inner enamel compartment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetics of cell proliferation of the IEE during normal and abnormal eruption, and with the relationship between the rate of cell proliferation and the rate of tooth eruption.
the kinetics of cell production in a tissue that is undergoing rapid cell turnover and is subject to considerable variation in cell production rate.
the physiology of the continuously erupting rat incisor and its inner enamel epithelum (IEE) which forms the enamel organ of the tooth.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the rate of tooth eruption is directly proportional to the rate of cell division in the IEE, and that the latter is regulated by the rate of cell loss from the basal lamina.
the IEE cell production is the rate limiting step in the eruption process.

, under conditions of high impedement, the rate of cell division of the IEE decreases, the generation time of the IEE cells increases, the proliferative compartment decreases in size, the cell production decreases, and the rate of eruption decreases.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the rate of eruption is controlled by the rate of cell proliferation in the IEE and that the latter is controlled by the amount of occlusal wear.
the rate of cell proliferation of the IEE is a function of the rate of eruption, the latter being the rate-limiting step in tooth growth.
the rate of tooth eruption is a direct function of the rate of cell proliferation in the IEE.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the rate of cell turnover in the inner enamel epithelial layer is a good predictor of the rate of eruption.
cell production in the rat incisor is regulated by the rate of tooth eruption, and not by the length of the IEE.
cell kinetics can be studied from measurements of eruption, a noninvasive technique, and that this method can be used in other studies of tooth eruption.
